newsitem.title: UK: British Steel head says stg rise must be reversed.
newsitem.headline: British Steel head says stg rise must be reversed.

text.p: The head of British Steel Plc warned that Britain could move "rapidly from apparent boom to recession" unless action was taken to reverse the rise in the value of sterling.

"The government and the Bank of England should be encouraged to say they think the pound is ludicrously overvalued," British Steel chairman and chief executive Sir Brian Moffat wrote in Thursday's Financial Times.
"And they should indicate they see no sense in further successive interest rate rises, which simply feed the import boom and fuel the high-street sales bonanza."
The pound has gained around 25 percent in value on a trade-weighted basis over the past year, punishing manufacturers trying to sell overseas.

British Finance Minister Gordon Brown reaffirmed his commitment to a "stable and competitive pound over the medium term" in an interview published in Thursday's Times newspaper. Brown said he would focus on pursuing consistent policies aimed at securing long-term growth.

The pound is now worth almost three marks, having gained 30 percent in value against the German currency over the past year. Moffat said anything above DM 2.50-2.60 was too high and argued that manufacturing jobs would be lost if there was no reduction.
He also said there was a case for delaying the planned launch of the single European currency in 1999 in order to bring Britain into the project.

British Steel last month reported a collapse in annual profits to 451 million pounds ($736.8 million) from 1.1 billion a year before as the strong pound hit home. The group has implemented a cost cutting and job reduction plan, with 2,000 redundancies this year.
